Highly urbanized communities benefit from synergistic interactions among commercial infrastructure and accommodation services; transitional medium urbanized communities are constrained by infrastructure-development mismatches that create facility gaps despite continued urban expansion; and low urbanized communities are dominated by ecological and topographic thresholds, where adverse interactions between transportation and river-network structures undermine recovery capacity. Field investigations and interviews with 12 stakeholders corroborate these patterns. By linking geographically weighted machine learning with locally grounded attribution analysis, the proposed framework provides a new pathway for uncovering spatially varying resilience mechanisms and translating them into place-based recovery strategies under increasing climate extremes.

candidates.title: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems
candidates.abstract: Performativity arises when prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, creating feedback between deployment and learning. This phenomenon occurs in policy-making and in self-evolving AI systems that shape their own future training data. Statistical inference is challenging because estimation errors in earlier predictors affect subsequent data distributions and propagate into later updates. We develop an end-to-end framework for statistical inference under performativity. For repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent, we establish central limit theorems at fixed deployment rounds and derive covariance recursions that capture both current-round sampling variation and uncertainty inherited from earlier deployments. We develop consistent covariance estimators using policy perturbations and score matching. These results can yield asymptotically valid confidence regions for population iterates and the performative stable point. We further extend prediction-powered inference to this dynamic setting, combining labeled observations with predictions on additional unlabeled data to improve statistical efficiency. We evaluate our framework in synthetic, semi-synthetic educational, and self-evolving large language model routing settings. Our experiments demonstrate that ignoring propagated uncertainty can lead to substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. Together, these results provide statistical tools for learning systems that help determine the distributions from which they learn. Our work establish a complete statistical inference under performativity, introducing new challenges and inference settings that we believe will provide substantial value to policy-making, statistics, and machine learning.

candidates.title: OmniMechanism Design for Human-AI Collaboration with Impressionable Minds
candidates.abstract: As AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, effectively integrating human expertise with AI outputs is critical for reliable decision-making. A substantial body of theoretical work studies optimal mechanisms for human-AI collaboration (HAC), focusing on when to involve humans and how to combine their expertise with AI predictions. However, these approaches largely overlook a key factor highlighted by empirical evidence: human judgments are impressionable and can vary depending on how AI outputs are presented. For example, when AI systems defer decisions to humans, revealing or withholding the AI prediction can significantly influence human judgments. Moreover, existing work neglects deployment-time variability, where conditions, particularly the cost of eliciting human input, may differ substantially from those observed during training. To address these challenges, we introduce a rigorous and theoretically grounded framework for human-AI collaboration, termed collaborative omnimechanism design, based on a novel and computationally efficient contextual bandit variant of boosting for outcome indistinguishability. In particular, we reduce a calibration-type outcome indistinguishability condition to weighted calibration, providing a novel time-efficiency result, bypassing the high-dimension curse induced by complicated collaboration methods and outcome space. Our framework provides a principled characterization of human impressionability and introduces a unified optimization scheme that enables robust and adaptable decision-making across diverse query costs and evaluation objectives without retraining. We evaluate the framework in three HAC settings, examining adaptation to query costs and prediction objectives without retraining, and show that its induced policies perform comparably to or better than the evaluated baselines.

candidates.title: CLiS: Plug-and-Play Attention Acceleration for Video Diffusion on TPUs via Certified Stabilization
candidates.abstract: High-resolution video diffusion relies on attention over long token sequences, making attention efficiency critical to generation latency. Our analysis identifies repeated maximum reductions and accumulator rescaling in online softmax as a bottleneck in long-context TPU attention. We propose CLiS (Certified Loop-invariant Stabilization), a training-free, plug-and-play optimization for video diffusion inference. CLiS fixes per-row stabilizers before the KV loop and certifies numerical safety per head, falling back to online softmax when certification fails. It integrates into existing fused-attention kernels without changing model weights or architecture. On Wan 2.2 and LTX-2 across TPU v6e and TPU7x, CLiS reduces diffusion transformer (DiT) step latency by up to 19.6% relative to tuned online softmax without measurable quality loss. Controlled TPU adaptations of prior GPU stabilization methods show performance or numerical-safety limitations. Preliminary causal LLM experiments also show up to 13.5% higher training throughput in continued pretraining and 7.7% in supervised fine-tuning.

candidates.title: Quantiles, Not Points: Streaming Quantile Matching for Ordinal-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration
candidates.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge scores are often distributionally shifted from human ratings on any given evaluation task, and post-hoc calibration (mapping LLM to human scores in a small labeled anchor set) has become a popular method to correct for this shift. In this paper we derive the calibration from two positions: that LLMaJ scores are ordinal ratings drawn from a distribution rather than isolated points. We present streaming quantile matching (SQM), a version of a classical method not previously bench marked for LLMaJ calibration, which is built on the two positions by computing the optimal-transport map between the LLM and human score distributions. We develop an evaluation framework and within it we show that unlike point-wise calibrations, SQM respects the ordinality of the human anchor set and achieves the best distributional fidelity and the top overall rank across models and data. We also show that in general, post-hoc calibration narrows the raw error gap between smaller and larger judge models, which opens the possibility of more efficient LLM judges.

candidates.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
candidates.abstract: Learning the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems relies on trajectory-based objectives, which require simulating the learned dynamics during training and backpropagating through the numerical scheme, at a cost that grows with the rollout horizon. We show that trajectory-based objectives degenerate as the rollout horizon increases, hindering gradient-based optimization, and that the numerical scheme biases the learned dynamics by constraining the spectrum of the learned Jacobian to its absolute stability region. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free objective that relies on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collocation, and approximates the velocity population risk to second order in the sampling step. We develop a theoretical framework for velocity-based learning, introducing stability estimates that control trajectory errors in terms of velocity errors, which enable us to establish universal and continuous-time approximation results when the learned velocity field is parameterized by deep neural networks. Building on a bias-variance decomposition of the VM objective, we show that its higher-order approximation of the velocity population risk yields a consistent minimizer; that it relates to the residual of an A-stable continuous-stage Runge-Kutta scheme, thus connecting VM to implicit integration without requiring any implicit solve; and that it implicitly matches the action of the learned Jacobian to that of the true one along the observed trajectories, without requiring access to the underlying velocity field or its Jacobian. Numerical experiments on nonlinear ordinary differential equations and semi-discretized time-dependent partial differential equations show that VM improves accuracy over trajectory-based objectives, while avoiding both the cost of simulation and the instabilities of long rollouts.

candidates.title: Compositional Self-Improvement: Promises and Pitfalls
candidates.abstract: Although self-improvement is becoming increasingly important as tasks become more complex, models struggle to generate reliable supervision for harder, out-of-distribution instances. One way to address this challenge is to exploit compositional structure: models often solve simpler subproblems more reliably than full problems, so their subproblem predictions can be composed into supervision for harder ones. We systematically study when this kind of composed supervision supports self-improvement and when it fails. Our controlled experiments identify three failure modes: unreliable subproblem predictions, errors introduced by composition, and limited supervision coverage. Beyond controlled settings, these findings carry over to more realistic coding and reasoning tasks: composed labels are more accurate than direct self-generated labels and improve performance even on compositions longer than those seen during training, while the failure modes remain visible. Further, although these failure modes often keep compositional self-improvement from fully succeeding on its own, a short SFT warmup with compositional self-improvement can bootstrap reinforcement learning on tasks that require composing skills the model already has, particularly when direct exploration rarely succeeds. Together, these findings characterize when compositional self-improvement can provide sufficiently reliable supervision to expand model capabilities.

candidates.title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

candidates.title: PRISM-Net: Dynamic Routing Network with VLM-Guided Disentangled Attribute Distillation for Explainable Fine-Grained Product Retrieval
candidates.abstract: Fine-grained visual product retrieval in large-scale e-commerce multimedia systems demands discriminative representations capable of simultaneously resolving macro-level category semantics and micro-level visual attributes such as structural contour (line) and chromatic appearance (color). However, conventional backbones including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision Transformers (ViTs) inherently suffer from feature entanglement and shortcut learning. To learn the micro-level visual attributes without costly manual attribute annotations, we propose phase-routed interpretable semantic mixture-of-experts network (PRISM-Net), an explainable multi-expert architecture that disentangles holistic visual features into disentangled line and color expert pathways governed by a conditional meta-router. In phase 1, we introduce an external VLM-Guided sigmoid semantic distillation mechanism with gradient-detached routing gates, utilizing zero-shot text prompts from SigLIP to supervise specialized structural and chromatic experts. In phase 2, the disentangled expert embeddings are adaptively fused with macro base features via a learned meta-router gate to calibrate category boundaries. Extensive 5-fold cross-validation across 275,454 e-commerce images (18 categories) and full-scale retrieval benchmarks (55,091 queries against a 220,363-image gallery) across SwinV2, ConvNeXt-V2, and DINOv3 demonstrate substantial gains. On SwinV2, PRISM-Net boosts full-fold product mAP@10 from 80.98% to 83.90% (+2.92%), line mAP@10 by +5.74%, and color mAP@10 by +9.12%. Furthermore, unsupervised distribution analysis of the meta-router gate reveals that both ViT and CNN backbones emergently allocate up to 6.8x higher structural line weights to rigid appliances and hardware while dedicating >96% chromatic weight to clothing.

candidates.title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance. In this study, we evaluate fourteen current models from six leading providers, one smaller and one larger model from each provider with two additional open-weight models, on 3,076 questions from four medical benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MedBullets) under standard multiple choice, the same questions with the answer choices withheld, and reconstruction of a hidden question from its choices alone. In the standard multiple-choice setting, the strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline on MedQA-USMLE and PubMedQA, but the smaller models trail their larger models by 8.7 percentage points and only two of the six pass the human-expert bar on the licensing examination. Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models. On memorization, the strongest models reconstruct one question in four from the answer choices alone, yet accuracy holds on the questions they cannot reconstruct. We further weigh accuracy against inference cost and test whether ensembling several models improves medical question answering.

candidates.title: Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
candidates.abstract: Agent harnesses govern how language models act in an environment; designing their policies by hand is difficult, while automated techniques require representative datasets and costly executions. We present Exo, an agent runtime architecture for safe learning during ongoing work that collapses the optimization loop into task execution, allowing agents to revise both their harness and their strategies for further improvement. A minimal protected mechanism layer preserves execution history and governs policy activation while the harness evolves through inspectable code changes. On long-running objectives in an open-world game, Exo reduces model cost by 12-53% relative to Codex and Pi in standalone runs and 45-82% in transfer runs, while matching task completion rates. Compared with the same starting policy without the ability to edit policy, Exo reduces held-out model cost by 35-61% on AppWorld and SREGym with comparable correctness, cutting AppWorld's mean task time by 13% and SREGym's median diagnosis time by 35%. On Continual Learning Bench coding tasks, model cost including learning falls by 14%, with both policies resolving every issue.

candidates.title: Compression Technique Interactions in Small Language Models: A Factorial Ablation Study
candidates.abstract: Deploying small language models on resource-constrained hardware requires compression, yet practitioners lack systematic guidance on how quantization, pruning, and post-compression recovery interact when combined. We present a factorial ablation study evaluating 72 compression configurations across four SLM architectures (2.7B-7B parameters), extended with a 48-configuration ordering analysis, benchmark accuracy validation on 30 compressed models, and robustness checks including multi-seed validation and full-corpus perplexity evaluation. INT8 quantization is effectively lossless (<0.5% accuracy degradation), while NF4 quantization combined with L1 magnitude pruning causes model collapse in all 16 tested combinations. LoRA-based fine-tuning reduces degraded perplexity by up to 97% after aggressive pruning; an ablation against standard fine-tuning without a teacher model shows the recovery is driven by LoRA adaptation itself rather than the distillation signal. Compression ordering shows no significant effect among viable configurations (ANOVA p = 0.96) but determines viability for NF4+pruning combinations. INT8 quantization alone provides 40-45% memory reduction with no quality loss. On-device CPU deployment via llama.cpp confirms these findings transfer off the GPU: 4-bit quantization runs 46-54% faster than 8-bit for a perplexity difference under 0.5 points, while un-structured pruning yields no CPU latency or memory benefit, consistent with its dense storage format.

candidates.title: Stochastic learning flow: moment equations for stochastic gradient descent at finite step size
candidates.abstract: Analytical theories of learning in deep networks often assume gradient flow, discarding the finite step size and batch noise of stochastic gradient descent (SGD). Starting from the discrete update, we derive continuous-time equations for the mean and covariance of the parameter distribution under a Gaussian closure for a general stochastic learning, to first order in the learning rate $\eta$. Applying these stochastic learning flow (SLF) equations to SGD, we show that the mean descends an effective loss regularized by the covariance and loss curvature, while the covariance, unlike in stochastic differential equation approximations, becomes unstable at curvature $2/\eta$. In SGD ensembles of linear and nonlinear networks, SLF predicts learning curves and mean trajectories more accurately than gradient flow and captures the covariance dynamics, failing where the parameter distribution becomes strongly non-Gaussian. In the full-batch limit, the edge of stability corresponds to a stationary point of the coupled sharpness-covariance dynamics, recovering self-stabilization and central flow, and batch-to-batch curvature fluctuations lower this threshold under SGD.

candidates.title: Few Trials, Many Metrics: Beta Mixtures for Low-Budget AI Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Evaluating a stochastic AI system often requires many repeated samples per instance, especially for metrics defined over long horizons. Recent work has shown that modeling instance-level success probabilities with a Beta distribution recovers Pass@$k$ from far fewer samples than direct estimation. We show that this framework supports a broader range of evaluation targets. We fit a mixture of Beta distributions by marginal maximum likelihood, with the number of components chosen by BIC. From that one fit, we compute Pass$^k$ and AUC@$k$ at any horizon in closed form. We also derive delta-method confidence intervals for these metrics and for Pass@$k$, which require no additional model calls. Treating configurations rather than tasks as instances extends the same model to sensitivity analysis. For repeated success metrics, we find that mixture priors yield more accurate estimators than naive estimation across competition mathematics and graduate-level science benchmarks when extrapolating beyond the observed number of trials, and the resulting intervals cover the full-data reference. When prompts are treated as instances, it estimates the distribution of prompt sensitivity more accurately than a comparable item-response baseline without external covariates. Direct estimators remain preferable once trials reach the target horizon.

candidates.title: Ensemble Classification and Cancer-Specific Gene Signatures from Quality-Aware Hybrid Gene Selection in TCGA RNA-Seq data
candidates.abstract: Gene-expression classifiers of cancer type are usually developed and validated within one cohort using random splits. Starting from a quality-aware hybrid Boruta selector from earlier work, we developed and evaluated ensemble classifiers and cancer-specific gene signatures. Using 10,469 TCGA tumours of 33 types, we compared five learners and three ensembles under decision rules fixed in advance, reran the selection in site-grouped cross-validation, transferred a breast-cancer subtype panel to 3273 tumours of the independent SCAN-B cohort, and built five-gene stage~I tumour versus adjacent-normal panels for nine cancer types. Logistic regression (LR) was the most accurate and best-calibrated single learner (balanced accuracy 0.943 on the locked test set). Stacking added at most 0.006 with 1000 genes but improved on LR in every fold with a minimal 100-gene panel; a hierarchical model did not reduce within-group confusion. Site-grouped validation lowered balanced accuracy by 0.027, almost entirely in colon and rectal cancer (0.008 without them and the untestable LAML). On SCAN-B, the subtype panel reached 0.855, close to the 50 PAM50 genes (0.876). Stage~I panels reached ROC AUC >= 0.99 in held-out patients and detected most later-stage tumours. Ensembles help most with a minimal panel; with 1000 genes, a calibrated linear model suffices.

candidates.title: Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes
candidates.abstract: Land-cover maps classified from wide-area hyperspectral surveys are least reliable along class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, so their errors are spatially structured. We study how this structure can direct a limited verification budget: when a low-altitude UAV or a ground crew can visit only a handful of sites, where it should go depends on how classifier uncertainty is arranged across the scene and how a fixed sensor footprint tiles that arrangement. We estimate a per-pixel uncertainty surface from the disagreement of an ensemble of spectral classifiers and select sites by greedy, field-of-view-aware coverage of the uncertainty mass. On seven benchmark scenes, the highest-uncertainty decile of pixels is 2.6 to 7.9 times richer in errors than the scene as a whole, and the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of the classifier's errors with 15 sites, 1.7 to 18 times as many as uncertainty-agnostic sampling of the same labelled region. A non-overlapping selection of the footprints richest in uncertainty does equally well, so the gain comes from scoring whole footprints by uncertainty mass. The advantage persists under spatially blocked evaluation and with a spectral-spatial classifier, although disagreement then ranks errors less well. It requires restricting the surface to labelled land cover: over the whole scene, disagreement peaks on unlabelled ground, where inspections cannot be scored. The best policy for covering connected high-uncertainty regions depends on the scene and on the threshold that defines them, and Gaussian-process selection covers less uncertainty than the coverage greedy on every scene. The pipeline runs on commodity CPUs.

candidates.title: A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks
candidates.abstract: The absolute trajectory error (ATE) is the standard measure of camera-motion accuracy, from SLAM to feed-forward 3D reconstruction. On the common Sintel protocol, a constant-velocity straight line using no images has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code. Two properties of ATE's alignment explain this. First, it maps any constant-velocity prediction onto the best-fitting line through the true path, so the line scores the path's regression residual. A residual signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion predicts when moving a prediction towards its constant-velocity fit lowers ATE. It gives the outcome for 95% of 1056 model-clip pairs, 98% of 792 held-out pairs and 97% of 1034 ScanNet pairs, and it separates Sintel (median SNR 0.86) from TUM, ScanNet and full-length Bonn and Wild-SLAM (2.7 to 27), where straightening raises every model's mean ATE. Second, position-only alignment ignores where cameras look: rotating a trajectory by 30 degrees against its orientations leaves ATE unchanged, yet worsens the reprojection of static points for every model on Sintel, TUM and ScanNet in the main setting, and the line, second by mean ATE on Sintel, places them worst by geometric mean: a lower ATE need not mean better geometry. Fitting the alignment's rotation to the predicted orientations gives pose-anchored ATE, a one-function change in ATE's units costing 0.17 ms per clip (ATE: 0.11 ms). It ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel, tracks the reprojection error under rotation and straightening, where ATE does not (Spearman 0.61 vs. 0.32), largely preserves the models' order, and ties 10-frame translational relative pose error (RPE) and the discernible trajectory error (DTE) on our rotation and reference tests. Code, predictions and results will be released.

candidates.title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
candidates.abstract: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions. Even so, a marginal test ranks expert-labelled direct above not-direct pairs within each action (AUROC 0.658) better than every null we built, so the panel does carry information about which pairs are direct. Tuned discovery methods, in configurations feasible at this panel size, recover less of it than a simple pairwise cross-correlation when pairs are ranked within each action, and no more when they are ranked within each target, which removes what the target alone predicts. Most direct pairs (132 of 222) involve actions below the support needed for 80% power against a 0.1-SD effect. For flow targets, conditioning on the target's other expert-labelled parents, often filed alongside the action, erodes the marginal discrimination, and most not-direct associations survive it: even with the graph's parent sets supplied, the expected separation does not emerge. For each property, we give a diagnostic computable before any discovery method is run.

candidates.title: Integer-Exact Microscaling: Running MXFP4 Language Models on INT8 Matrix Units
candidates.abstract: On hardware whose fastest matrix datapath is INT8$\times$INT8, such as the Neural Accelerators of Apple's M5 GPUs, 4-bit weights must become INT8 operands. Existing MXFP4 kernels already map FP4 (E2M1) values to integers by doubling them, but apply every 32-element block scale inside the reduction. We show when no per-block work is needed: a row of MXFP4 weights is exactly one INT8 vector times one power-of-two scale if its block exponents span at most three, so a linear layer becomes a single INT8 GEMM with one rescale per output. Enforcing the condition adds at most 1/16 of a row's largest rounding error to the blocks it changes, and real weights already satisfy it: 97.9-99.97% of rows across seven models, including 99.93% of the 95M rows of a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. The resulting spread-constrained MXFP4 files stay standard MXFP4. With integer instead of power-of-two block multipliers, an integer-exact format (16-wide blocks, multipliers 1..10, 4.26 bits) runs as one exact INT8 GEMM and is more accurate than NVFP4 (4.5 bits) with its standard scale rule on five small models, within 0.06 perplexity of NVFP4 with scale search. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's routed experts with INT8 activations it is as close to the FP8 model as NVFP4 with scale search (KL divergence 0.0557 vs. 0.0553) and closer than MLX's MXFP4 and affine INT4; with every matrix quantized it solves 94.8% of GSM8K vs. 91.0% for MLX's MXFP4. Quantizing only the 74k routed expert matrices (96% of the parameters) to either of our formats with INT8 activations costs at most 0.2% perplexity. A complete W4A8 system on the M5 produces outputs bit-identical to the quantized reference; prefill is 1.34-1.74x faster than MLX on a dense model, 1.10-1.57x on two MoE models up to 35B parameters and 1.22-1.29x on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, where shared non-GEMM work bounds the gain.

candidates.title: VoirDire: Counterfactual Calibration for Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge Aggregation
candidates.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge systems often aggregate multiple judges to improve evaluation reliability. However, judge agreement can reflect shared biases toward verbosity, formatting, or fluency rather than the intended evaluation target. Addressing these shared biases is challenging because observational judge outputs alone cannot distinguish agreement driven by target quality from agreement driven by nuisance attributes. We introduce VoirDire, an intervention-calibrated aggregation method for LLM-judge panels. VoirDire applies controlled interventions that vary specified surface attributes while aiming to preserve the evaluation target; it then uses paired changes in judge scores to identify nuisance-sensitive directions. It attenuates these directions and selects aggregation weights that retain variation across items while penalizing sensitivity to the interventions, making the final consensus less dependent on superficial features. We show theoretically that observational judge outputs alone cannot identify which shared direction is target-relevant, while paired interventions provide the contrast needed to identify nuisance-sensitive variation. We evaluate VoirDire on 12 datasets spanning continuous scoring, binary classification, and pairwise preference. Compared with the existing LLM-judge aggregation baselines, VoirDire reduces MAE by up to 26.8% on continuous-score tasks and improves accuracy by up to 5.3 percentage points on binary and preference tasks. These findings suggest that counterfactual interventions provide an additional means of improving the reliability and controllability of LLM-based evaluation beyond merely relying on observed judge agreement.

candidates.title: Swap, Replicate, Read the Mass: A Protocol for Auditing Demographic Bias in System One Decision Models
candidates.abstract: System One decision models replace text generation with typed, probability-scored answers and are entering production. Answers execute without a person in the loop, and no multi-model audit exists on established bias benchmarks. We provide that audit: three benchmarks: BBQ (all eleven categories), CrowS-Pairs, and SilverSpoon, adapted to the typed interface, twelve models plus a no-thinking ablation, and 1,638,000 decisions. Every order-sensitive item runs twice with options swapped; native typed models also swap labels; ten configurations repeat under extra seeds and batch 16. We find widespread stereotype alignment, order-dependent answers, and confidence that tracks instability rather than bias. In BBQ, 97 of 143 model-by-category scores are significant and 94 aligned, while the commercial reference abstains on 99.5% of ambiguous items, hiding aligned probability mass. Option swaps flip 0.0% to 72.6% of choices; typed scoring stays below 10% except Laya (22-33%), and untuned letter prompting reaches 73%. CrowS-Pairs preference spans 0.496 to 0.816, and boolean answers can be decided by position (1.00 versus 0.005). SilverSpoon judgments shift toward lower-SES labels in five of eight decision models, inherited from the 9B backbone or induced by tuning. Audits must permute options and reverse questions by default; order-invariant scoring should become a procurement requirement.

candidates.title: Where Does EEG Help Wearable Freezing of Gait Detection?
candidates.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) detectors built on inertial measurement units (IMUs) are accurate while the legs move, but they become unreliable when the legs are nearly still, which is exactly when akinetic freezing, voluntary stopping, and standing must be told apart. Electroencephalography (EEG) captures motor-planning activity that leg sensors cannot, but EEG is impractical for daily use. We ask where EEG helps: as an input at inference time, or only during pretraining, so that the deployed detector still needs only IMUs. We assemble a pretraining corpus of synchronized EEG and IMU recordings (5 datasets, 184 people, 94 hours) and compare six settings that differ only in the modalities used for pretraining and as model input, each with tuned hyperparameters and five independent pretraining runs. On the BXHC FoG dataset (leave-one-patient-out, 10 patients with FoG), adding EEG as input raises FoG F1 from 0.663 to 0.740 (9 of 10 patients improve), and the gain in ranking performance is confined to the quartile of windows with the least leg movement (AUROC +0.063). Pretraining the IMU encoder jointly with EEG improves an IMU-only detector both within the cohort (FoG F1 0.663 to 0.705) and when it is trained on a small cohort and tested on another (FoG F1 +0.083, all 10 test patients improve). Repeating the study with PD-only and healthy-only pretraining corpora, each with its own hyperparameter search, shows that IMU-based detection is robust to the corpus, whereas the benefit of aligning EEG with IMU requires both. Cross-cohort analysis further shows that detectors trained without annotated voluntary stops classify nearly all stops as freezing. Finally, on PD versus non-PD classification in three external datasets, joint EEG+IMU pretraining improves PD detection from walking EEG over EEG-only pretraining (AUROC 0.750 vs. 0.683), while IMU-based detection does not depend on the pretraining.

candidates.title: Knowing Where to Look: Interactive Object Search via Spatial-Semantic Fusion
candidates.abstract: When searching for an object, humans naturally combine semantic intuition - reasoning about where the object is likely to be stored - with geometric awareness of what parts of the space are visible, occluded, or unexplored. Effective robot object search requires the same joint reasoning, yet existing methods rely on only one: geometric methods maintain principled spatial beliefs but lack deep semantic understanding, while language-model based methods leverage commonsense knowledge but maintain no explicit belief over space. We argue that jointly reasoning over semantic and geometric evidence in an explicit 3D belief enables human-like interactive object search that outperforms either modality alone. To test this claim, we build a system that accumulates per-object VLM plausibility scores and geometric occupancy evidence via Bayesian log-odds filtering into a unified 3D voxel belief field. High-belief regions in the combined belief field drive action selection at each step: taking a closer look from a different viewpoint, navigating toward an unexplored region of the workspace, or physically interacting with a closed cabinet. We deploy this system end-to-end on a bimanual mobile humanoid and find that it outperforms geometry-only search and LLM-based planning methods. Project website - https://skymanaditya1.github.io/objsearch-website/

candidates.title: Robustness Starts with the Objective: Designing and Certifying Robust LLM-Generated Heuristics
candidates.abstract:
LLMs are increasingly used to design heuristics for computer systems. However, most synthesis frameworks evaluate candidates by their average performance, which can mask severe regressions on specific workloads. Even adding adversarial training inputs doesn't eliminate these regressions, and percentile objectives (e.g., optimizing for the 95th percentile) overlook how severe regressions can be beyond the selected threshold.
  We present TAILOR, a framework that guides LLM synthesis using the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the cost difference between each candidate and an existing baseline on the same workload. This paired CVaR measures the average difference over the worst fraction of workloads. We show that a negative paired CVaR guarantees improvements in both average performance and tail optimality gap relative to the unknown optimum, without ever computing that optimum.
  We find that TAILOR achieves the best mean--tail trade-off among the synthesis objectives we evaluate across three case studies: Azure GPU batch admission, Azure VM packing, and server placement. Tested across seven diverse optimization benchmarks, TAILOR produces heuristics that are certified with 99% confidence to improve both average performance and tail optimality gaps over the baseline in six of them. On these six benchmarks, TAILOR also outperforms known robust, human-designed alternatives in the tail while achieving better or comparable average-performance improvement over the baseline.

candidates.title: To Jev or Not to Jev: When Can System-1 Decision Models Replace LLM Judges?
candidates.abstract: Decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer typed questions about a text (yes/no, multiple choice, or an ordinal score) with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass and without generating text, which makes them an inexpensive candidate for LLM-as-a-judge workloads. We evaluate 14 System-1 decision models, selected with a pre-stated protocol, against four generative judges (Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.6 with and without reasoning, and Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking) on eleven established judge benchmarks. Five of the 14 are statistically indistinguishable from GPT-5.6 without reasoning on all five pairwise and best-of-4 benchmarks, and the two strongest, DReX-Max and d1-ultra, are significantly more accurate than Haiku on JudgeBench, LLMBar and RewardBench 2. Conditioned on a reference answer generated once per prompt, eleven models reach 90.3-93.4% on JudgeBench, statistically indistinguishable from Opus 5.5 and GPT-5.6 with reasoning, and on PPE best-of-16 every reference-guided System-1 judge matches GPT-5.6 with reasoning at roughly one-sixteenth of its cost per prompt. Several System-1 judges are better calibrated than every generative judge and correlate more strongly with human helpfulness ratings. Robustness to instructions injected into the judged response is a property of the individual model rather than of the System-1 design: an appended note to the evaluator reverses 0-5% of the correct verdicts of five models but 17-49% for the other nine. Two general System-1 leaderboards that contain no judging tasks predict judging accuracy (Pearson r = 0.95-0.96), a well-calibrated System-1 first stage matches Opus on LLMBar while escalating 17% of items, and same-size controls show that the correctness deficit of a 4B decision model is a reasoning gap rather than a size gap.

candidates.title: Selecting or Solving? What Best-of-N Verification Delivers in Video Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Answering a complex question about a long video is a grounding problem: the answer turns on a few seconds of evidence, and vision-language models remain well below human accuracy at finding them. The standard way to spend extra test-time compute on this kind of video reasoning is best-of-N selection: sample several chain-of-thought answers from a fixed model, then let a second model re-watch the video and pick one. Such pipelines are reported by a single headline number, their margin over a majority vote. That number conflates two effects with opposite deployment consequences: the benefit the second model adds by selecting among candidates, and the benefit it would have supplied by solving the question itself. We separate them, measuring the Selection Increment (SI) -- selection accuracy minus the same verifier's accuracy with the candidates withheld -- alongside the margin over self-consistency, across five long-video benchmarks. The Selection Increment is largest for the weakest verifiers: a verifier that solves poorly on its own leaves the candidates the most room to help. Beating the majority vote follows the opposite profile: where the vote already sits near its ceiling no verifier we test improves on it; below that ceiling only the strongest do. On Video-Holmes, the two come apart on a single pool of candidates -- a weak verifier gains +19.3 points from the candidates yet lands 7.1 points below the vote, while the frontier verifier gains the least and beats the vote. The weakest verifier also shows a failure mode: on EgoSchema it picks by where an option sits in the list rather than by what the video shows. Read as a merit score, SI puts a verifier that fails to beat a majority vote at the top of its ranking; read as an audit, it says which of the two effects a headline number delivers. Code is available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/best-n-selection-video-reasoning.

candidates.title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

candidates.title: Beyond Blackwell: Constrained Data Processing Inequalities
candidates.abstract:
We study the comparison of statistical experiments from a decision-theoretic standpoint, working with Markov transitions as basis-free linear maps on dual spaces. Our starting observation is that the data-processing inequality, that adding noise to an experiment cannot lower its Bayes risk, is the functoriality of fibrewise minimisation over a presheaf of decision rules: the rules available after an experiment form a presheaf, garbling acts on it by precomposition, and a risk functional is a natural transformation from it to the ordered reals. The argument refers to neither probabilities nor expected values, and it survives replacing the decision presheaf by a sub-presheaf of admissible rules. Any constraint imposed on the strategy that a rule induces fairness, unbiasedness, is automatically of this form, and so yields a data-processing inequality with no counterpart in the unconstrained Blackwell theory.
  Our main result is their quantitative companion. For constraints closed under post-processing we define a constrained deficiency and prove a constrained randomization theorem: one experiment dominates another on every admissible decision problem exactly when the constrained deficiency is small. The classical theorem is the case of no constraint, where the identity is itself an admissible rule; in general it is not, and the constrained deficiency is an optimisation over the coarsenings of an experiment that render it compliant. Specialising to equalized odds, we exhibit a pair of experiments that unconstrained Bayes risk identifies at a given loss and prior but that the constrained risk separates, giving a one-line certificate of Blackwell-incomparability. We work throughout with finite sets.

candidates.title: Efficient and Scalable Multi-View Masked Autoencoder for Heterogeneous Graph Self-Supervised Learning
candidates.abstract: Recent years have witnessed the flourishing of self-supervised learning on heterogeneous graphs, e.g., masked autoencoder-based methods. However, existing methods suffer from three issues, including the prohibitive computational cost of constructing meta-path-induced subgraphs, the limitations of uniform random masking, and the suboptimal objective of reconstructing potentially noisy or uninformative original node features. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-View Masked Auto Encoder (MVMAE), a novel, efficient, and scalable framework for heterogeneous graph self-supervised learning. First, MVMAE introduces a novel multi-view mask-then-reconstruct strategy. Instead of masking individual nodes or features, MVMAE randomly masks entire meta-path views and guides the model to reconstruct their representations from remaining visible views. This approach shifts the learning objective to a high-level and semantic task, providing a more robust and informative supervisory signal that is effective even when initial node features are absent or flawed. Then, to handle the computational demands, MVMAE employs an efficient offline aggregation mechanism that pre-computes and reuses representations for each meta-path view, completely avoiding the costly construction of meta-path-induced subgraphs. Next, to fuse the representations of each view, MVMAE uses a Transformer-based multi-view fusion encoder to capture the complex correlations between views, and a deliberately simple MLP decoder to compel the encoder to learn highly expressive and robust node representations. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets, including three large-scale graphs, demonstrate that MVMAE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art self-supervised and even semi-supervised baselines, confirming its superior effectiveness and scalability. Our source code is released at https://github.com/hcmdgh/MVMAE.

candidates.title: WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Most agentic robotic systems use vision-language models (VLMs) either to orchestrate predefined skills or to directly generate actions, constraints, and control programs. The former is limited by the available skill library, while the latter requires VLMs to reason about precise geometry and contact. In this paper, we propose WorldSketch, a new paradigm for agentic robotics in which a VLM constructs a world model rather than generating robot actions. The VLM acts as an agent that actively queries perception tools to build and visually validate a minimal kinematic world model, capturing only task-relevant objects, their interaction geometry, and possible motions. A geometric planner then jointly optimizes contact and whole-body motion on the resulting model. Moreover, the world model is self-improving: execution feedback verifies outcomes, updates uncertain hypotheses, and enables the agent to revise the model when its predictions are contradicted. We demonstrate the generality of this paradigm across RoboCasa, LIBERO-PRO, and R2R-CE navigation, achieving zero-shot success rates of 91%, 97%, and 76%, respectively. On RoboCasa, WorldSketch outperforms the next-best zero-shot agent baseline by 58 percentage points while using 10 times fewer VLM input tokens; on LIBERO-PRO, it exceeds CaP-X by 82 percentage points. In navigation, it matches the success rate of step-by-step VLM agents while using 6 times fewer input tokens.

candidates.title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
candidates.abstract: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious. An analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning while extracting the specification can do worse than no intervention, and instructing it to ignore them did not close the gap, so we exclude assistant turns structurally. On Lost in Conversation (replaying difficulty-selected instances), where AO is an oracle by construction, AC3 closes 55-84% of the gap between full context and AO on three of four tasks and exceeds AO on the fourth, and an LLM that faithfully summarizes the history does not reproduce the gain even with more compute. On real WildChat conversations, a GPT-5-mini judge prefers AC3's next turn over both full context and AO in every configuration of our main table, though this preference depends on the judge; on CollabLLM results are mixed. In stateful tool use (tau2-bench), AO collapses to 0% on every model; AC3 does not collapse, though it falls slightly behind full context. Detector studies show that Reset removes injected pollution but is not span-selective: the gain comes from rebuilding the specification.

candidates.title: Behavioral Steering of Vision-Language-Action Models in the Low-Parameter Regime
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to adapt pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs). We investigate the problem of behavioral steering: adapting a VLA's execution style to preferences such as carrying objects higher. To investigate how little trainable capacity such steering requires and how much pretrained capability can be retained, we freeze an OpenVLA-OFT 7B policy and optimize TinyLoRA adapters with 8 to 384 trainable parameters using either policy-gradient RL (GRPO) or evolutionary search (CMA-ES). With just 256 trainable parameters, we raise carry height by 120 mm on trained tasks at 92% success and by 74 mm on a held-out task at 80% success. By rescaling the learned update, we can tune the trade-off between style gains and capability retention without retraining. Increasing adapter capacity generally improves this trade-off, retaining more pretrained capability at comparable style gains. The choice of optimizer also depends on capacity, with CMA-ES being competitive at low parameter counts, while GRPO offers better trade-offs as capacity grows. These findings show that extremely low-dimensional updates can steer pretrained VLA behavior, with adapter capacity, optimizer choice, and update scaling offering practical control over adaptation and retention.

candidates.title: SASFormer: Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
candidates.abstract: All-in-one image restoration aims to recover high-quality images from multiple degradation types using a single unified model. Recent methods improve unified restoration with hybrid attention, prompt learning, or routing mechanisms, but generally focus on enhancing degradation adaptivity while employing similar feature modeling strategies across network stages. Consequently, the distinct representation requirements of encoding and decoding under diverse degradations remain insufficiently explored. In this paper, we propose SASFormer, a Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for all-in-one blind image restoration. SASFormer follows a stage-aware design principle: the encoder uses established hybrid channel-spatial attention to build robust content-preserving and degradation-aware representations, while the decoder employs adaptive selective attention for restoration-oriented reconstruction. To address the stage-specific requirements of decoder reconstruction, we develop Adaptive Selective Channel Self-Attention (ASCSA) and Adaptive Selective Spatial Self-Attention (ASSSA), enabling the decoder to dynamically identify restoration-relevant channel responses and spatial contexts. Specifically, ASCSA performs adaptive query-channel selection and attention masking, while ASSSA adaptively integrates spatial attention across multiple window sizes. Compact implicit prompts further modulate the selection process without requiring explicit degradation labels. Extensive experiments on 3-, 5-, and 11-degradation settings demonstrate that SASFormer achieves strong restoration performance with favorable parameter efficiency. Moreover, stage-wise representation analysis and ablation studies provide empirical support for the proposed stage-aware design and the effectiveness of decoder-side adaptive selection.

candidates.title: Reflex: Fast Robot Policy Serving by Reusing and Correcting Past Actions
candidates.abstract:
Modern robot policies often perform expensive inference to generate action chunks, making serving a latency bottleneck for real-time control and a throughput bottleneck for multi-robot serving. Building on the success of caching in image, video, and audio generation, recent robot-policy advances have reported promising speedups by reusing intermediate denoising states to avoid redundant computation. Surprisingly, we find that such reuse often offers little advantage over simply running fewer denoising steps from fresh noise, without any cache. Moreover, accelerating denoising leaves the expensive policy backbone intact, which can account for 70% of GPU time.
  We present Reflex, a serving layer that turns past policy executions into a backbone-free path for future decisions. Rather than reusing intermediate computations, Reflex caches complete action chunks to bypass both the backbone and action head. This introduces two challenges: similar observations can demand different actions, and small action deviations (errors) in reuse can compound into execution stalls. Reflex addresses these through two-level cache correction. At the action level, it learns action-aware similarity from past policy decisions, assembles compatible chunks, and applies lightweight residual correction to limit action mismatch. At the execution level, it captures task progress and adaptively refreshes the original policy to limit accumulated errors and balance inference cost. Without modifying the underlying policy, Reflex improves inference latency by 1.4x to 11x and throughput by 2.0x to 2.2x on representative workloads and real robots, while preserving comparable task success.

candidates.title: 3D Neural Rendering for Automated Ultrasonic Laser Scans
candidates.abstract: Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

candidates.title: When Does Spatial Cooperation Help? Contamination Regimes in Decentralized Online Spectrum Anomaly Learning
candidates.abstract: Learning-based spectrum monitors adapt online to benign propagation changes, but persistent rogue transmissions can gradually become incorporated into the learned background. Spatially distributed receivers provide additional evidence for detecting such anomalies, while decentralized model mixing can also spread contamination to receivers with clean measurements. We study this tradeoff using a decentralized online learner with sample gating and model sharing. We show that, without defenses, contamination propagation is governed by the occupancy rate and is independent of cross-receiver correlation. In contrast, the benefit of spatial fusion depends strongly on correlation and the detector operating point, so cooperation can either improve or degrade detection. We also show that fragmented transmissions can evade gating based on temporally smoothed statistics. Combining smoothed and per-sample gating substantially improves robustness to such intermittent contamination.

candidates.title: Gravitational Capture of Large Interstellar Planetesimals by Collapsing Prestellar Cores
candidates.abstract: We investigate the capture of free-floating planetesimals by the time-varying gravitational potential of a collapsing prestellar core. We use one-dimensional collapse models to estimate the volume of space from which planetesimals are captured. We combine this calculation with an estimate of the size distribution and velocity dispersion of the free-floating planetesimal population to determine the largest planetesimal that is typically captured, as well as the total mass of all planetesimals captured by a given protostar. We consider two cases: one in which the free-floating planetesimal population comes from the birth cluster of the star, and one in which the planetesimals are captured from the Galactic population of free-floating planetesimals. We find that the details of the collapse matter substantially, with the predicted diameter of the largest captured body from the Galactic population ranging from $2.8$ km to $6.4$ km depending on collapse model, and the largest body from our model birth cluster environment ranging from $70$ km to $1200$ km, for assumed velocity dispersions ranging from 0.7 to 8.5 km/s. The total solid mass captured by this mechanism does not exceed 0.07 Earth masses in all cases. We discuss the effect of these captured objects on the planet formation process, and argue that while the total solid mass captured is likely not significant, the largest captured bodies may grow to planet size via accretion of pebbles present in their host disks. This process may accelerate planet formation, or enable it in disks that have difficulty in forming their own planetesimals.

candidates.title: Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit
candidates.abstract: Imitation policies inherit the operator's pace, and re-timing the demonstrations to run faster works only until success collapses at two to three times demonstration speed. Recent methods attribute that collapse to distribution shift and answer it with finer rules for which segments may be sped up; we show it has a mechanical cause that segment selection cannot address. A low-level controller realises only a bounded displacement per control period, so merging consecutive commands produces sums outside that bound: training pairs that promise a transition the plant cannot deliver. The share of such pairs in the re-timed data, which we call the exceed share, tracks where the retrained policy collapses. The rule that follows has a single parameter: merge greedily while the sum stays realisable. Every command is then realisable by construction, the demonstrated geometry is preserved, and the speed-up lands only where the demonstrator left slack. On four simulated robomimic tasks, 200 held-out seeds per cell, a merge cap of two is at or above the frozen policy's success on all four, by 14 points on Square, and shortens the successful episodes. At matched tempo, uniform re-timing loses 9 and 16 points on Can and ToolHang, is within noise on the other two, and reaches zero on the hardest at 2x. Placement also matters: no shuffled, entropy-guided or speed-conditioned alternative beats the rule on three of the four tasks, by margins the exceed share alone does not explain; on the fourth, at a tempo the task absorbs, every placement lands in the same band. The same principle carries to a simulated humanoid whole-body tracker: re-timing 429 reference motions within its velocity envelope succeeds on 71% of clips at 2.3x, against 51% for uniform time scaling at 2x.

candidates.title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents extend their capabilities with skills, each with a name, a description, and a body. Under progressive disclosure, an LLM router selects skills by name and description alone and loads only the selected bodies. Skill libraries grow continually as users and agents add new skills. Because the router relies on this metadata, a similar new skill can displace an earlier one, breaking previously correct routing even though the earlier skill and the router are unchanged. This routing interference is aggravated for public skills, whose descriptions may not match their bodies. We formulate the problem as lifelong skill routing, a class-incremental continual learning problem. A solution must keep earlier skills selectable without suppressing new ones. Existing approaches fall short, since continually retraining the router risks catastrophic forgetting and rewriting methods either ignore similar skills or require per-skill feedback. We therefore propose Skill++, which rewrites only the name and description of each incoming skill, without router training or labeled data. The new description states what the body supports, how the skill differs from its closest predecessor, and what related work it excludes. As a library grows to 731 skills over ten sessions, Skill++ selects all required skills for 76.3% of queries, versus 36.4% under the original metadata. Across three benchmarks and five LLM routers, it outperforms all compared approaches, and its gains carry over to the Codex CLI agent harness.

candidates.title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberatio
candidates.abstract: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch substantially more often than margin-increasing con- trols. We then continue selected realized branches through the committee to distinguish textual persistence from preference and final-decision changes. The contribution is a controlled audit for local branch susceptibility in this specified protocol, not an estimate of deployment frequency, decision correct- ness, or a phenomenon unique to multi-agent systems.

candidates.title: Governing Equations of Human Sleep Macro-Structure:Symbolic Discovery from 1,106 Nights
candidates.abstract: Human sleep is organized into a small number of cycles per night: deep sleep dominates early cycles, REM lengthens toward morning, and light sleep clusters at cycle boundaries. These regularities have long been described qualitatively but never distilled into closed-form laws from large-scale data. A total of 1,106 nights (Sleep-EDF 153 + SHHS 953) are segmented into REM-anchored cycles, and four cycle-indexed statistics follow simple closed-form equations: cycle length declines nearly linearly (R^2=0.996), REM duration follows an inverted U (R^2=0.873), deep-sleep (N3) run length decays exponentially (R^2=0.987) with a time constant of 2.94 cycles, consistent with the homeostatic Process S of the two-process model, and light-sleep (N1) run length follows a U shape (R^2=0.956), confirming a "long-short-long" pattern across the night. The laws are reproduced by per-night differentiable fitting (142/142 and 773/773 nights converge), by unconstrained symbolic regression (PySR), and by a 500-night generative synthesizer built from them. Their robustness is established against the two main methodological threats: bootstrap CIs computed by resampling whole nights (1,000 replications) exclude zero for every shape term, and a five-level scan of the REM-merge segmentation threshold preserves every qualitative form. These appear to be the first closed-form laws governing the macro-structure of sleep, distilled and tested across an age-mixed sample (healthy young adults and community-based older adults).

candidates.title: RATR: Training-Free Material Rebinding via Role Assignment and Temporal Routing
candidates.abstract: Material rebinding aims to transfer the material appearance from a reference image while preserving the target object's geometry and identity. Existing methods typically struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation due to the coupled influence of structural and appearance cues in their visual conditions. We identify role entanglement in the target and reference conditions as a contributing factor the target condition carries both geometry and its original appearance while the reference condition contains material cues alongside object-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose RATR, a training-free material rebinding method built on a diffusion-based image editor that assigns complementary roles to the two conditions and coordinates their influence during denoising. To make the target condition primarily convey structure, we introduce an albedo-resolved surface release mechanism, which suppresses the target's original surface appearance while retaining geometric cues, yielding a structure-oriented condition for material transfer. On the reference side, the designed material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues while reducing interference from object-specific structure, yielding a complementary material-oriented condition.

candidates.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
candidates.abstract:
Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often requiring weeks of computation. In this work, we propose SFTProbe, a fundamentally different approach that bypasses this pipeline by directly predicting the quality of reasoning data.
  We show that a brief LoRA-based adaptation, combined with evaluating loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace, suffices to estimate both difficulty and diversity. SFTProbe is grounded in a geometric view of post-training, where pretrained LLMs lie in a low-rank, anisotropic loss basin. By probing this basin via low-rank perturbations, we construct compact loss signatures whose clustering captures diversity, while loss at curvature inflection points provides a robust proxy for difficulty. We also provide a simple criterion for teacher selection. Empirically, our approach reduces data curation time from weeks to hours while maintaining or improving performance. Remarkably, on mathematical reasoning, 5k generated examples match the highly filtered 89k-example in OpenThoughts-Math dataset, and 7.5k generated examples outperforms it by 2.5% in accuracy. We further introduce a high-quality physics reasoning dataset, and use it to train a model that outperforms an IPhO 2025 silver-medal-winning model. The code and the dataset are released at https://bigml-cs-ucla.github.io/SFTProbe-page/.

candidates.title: Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation
candidates.abstract: Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem. By unfolding the classical iterative solver, our network integrates physical consistency with dual-domain deep priors via learned transforms, soft thresholding, and exact data reinsertion. Within the learned prior, a spatial Restormer branch captures local waveform structures, while a fast Fourier convolution (FFC) branch extracts global context, effectively suppressing incoherent components and enhancing spectral energy concentration in the $f-k$ domain. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges these complementary features via bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation, yielding substantial interpolation improvements. To overcome the severe loss of lateral continuity caused by large gaps, we introduce structural similarity (SSIM) supervision, complemented by focal frequency loss (FFL) and transform consistency constraints to suppress incoherent high-frequency components and regularize training. Experiments on a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset under 50% random and consecutive trace removal demonstrate the effectiveness of SSI-POCS. It significantly enhances event continuity across large gaps and mitigates artifacts, achieving a 3.285~dB SNR improvement over the best competing method while reducing parameters by 75.66%.

candidates.title: TabAbax: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
candidates.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable in-context prediction on unseen tabular datasets without task-specific training. Mechanistic work has shown that increasing the depth of the ICL Transformer yields weak gains, leaving the main headroom for gains in the synthetic pretraining prior and column-row encoder upstream of the ICL backbone. We introduce TabAbax, a TFM built on TabICLv2 that focuses all modifications on these two upstream components. On the prior side, we further improve the quality and complexity of the synthetic pretraining prior. On the encoder side, a two-pass column-row stack strengthens cross-feature interactions before row compression, using learned Fourier scalar encoding from TabFM and Causilo. Evaluations on BeyondArena and TabArena show strong regression-centric gains: TabAbax reaches 1,238 Elo on the 142-dataset BeyondArena suite (10th of 41 evaluated methods), 1,676 Elo on TabArena's overall 51-dataset suite (11th of 99 methods, +115 over TabICLv2), and 2,024 Elo on TabArena's regression benchmark (7th of 99 methods, +336 over TabICLv2, +21 over TabFM). A prior-only ablation confirms the attribution: the improved prior alone yields +228 Elo for regression, demonstrating that prior quality is the dominant knob for improving regression performance.

candidates.title: WAR-CRAFT: Refining Web API Recommendations through Requirement Auditing
candidates.abstract: Web API recommenders return a set of APIs for a mashup request but do not check it against provider documentation, the main public evidence of an API's capabilities. The set can therefore contain unsupported or redundant APIs and miss requested capabilities. Filling every apparent gap does not fix this, because a gap may already be served, may not need its own API, or may have no documented provider. We study post-recommendation refinement, which revises a frozen recommender's output using only the request, the catalog, and provider documentation. We propose WAR-CRAFT, which treats refinement as three decisions. An LLM removes unsupported or subsumed APIs by judging candidates jointly, then audits the remaining set against a requirement checklist derived from the request. For each uncovered requirement, a fine-tuned catalog-constrained Resolver proposes a catalog API or abstains, and an independent documentation check admits only supported proposals. On ProgrammableWeb with 7 heterogeneous upstream recommenders, WAR-CRAFT raises mean SetF1 from 0.558 to 0.644, above the strongest of 5 refinement baselines (62.5%), and roughly halves functional redundancy (0.127 to 0.065) without changing mean functional coverage. Gains range from +2.2 points on generative recommenders to +18.2 on fixed-cutoff rankers. At matched set sizes, WAR-CRAFT still outperforms truncating the upstream output, so the gain is not explained by set-size calibration alone. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZsXu-enrico/WAR-CRAFT.

candidates.title: Structured Channel Network Pruning with Bi-Sparse Matrix Factorization
candidates.abstract: Structured channel pruning for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) plays an important role in pattern recognition and deep learning. Nevertheless, existing methods usually calculate channel importance scores based on the magnitudes of individual filters, making it difficult to distinguish shared redundancy from individual channel contributions. To tackle this limitation, we propose a novel structured channel pruning method termed bi-sparse matrix factorization (BSMF). Specifically, BSMF characterizes the convolutional weight matrix as output-channel coefficients over a shared basis with row-wise $\ell_{2,p}$-norm and column-wise $\ell_{2,q}$-norm regularization terms, respectively. Note that $p,q\in[0,1)$, which, to our best knowledge, has not been explored in the literature. To solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we develop an efficient update scheme built upon the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), in which all subproblems admit closed-form solutions. After that, a compact CNN is obtained by reconstructing the convolutional filters from the learned factors and discarding the redundant channels. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K datasets demonstrate that our proposed BSMF achieves significant network compression while maintaining high reconstruction accuracy. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/xianchaoxiu/BSMF

candidates.title: The First-Order Value of Free Covariates in Budgeted Risk Monitoring
candidates.abstract: A deployed model sees its inputs for free, but checking whether its risk has risen requires costly labels. We study how to spend a label budget so that a risk increase is detected quickly while false alarms stay controlled, including under input shifts that keep the risk below a safety threshold $\tau$. Let $A$ be the false-alarm control scale and $h(r)=\mathrm{kl}(r,\tau)$ the Bernoulli KL divergence between the changed risk $r$ and $\tau$. At label rate $b=c/\log A$, we prove that every rule that chooses requests from its own label history has worst-case (Lorden) delay at least $(1/h(r)+1/c)\log A$ to first order: besides collecting evidence, it must wait for its next label. The bound needs only a label budget on one finite stretch of safe source data and false-alarm control over an initial window; a bound on the average time to false alarm does not suffice. When a harmful change also shifts the inputs, a rule that lets the inputs trigger labeling attains delay $\log A/h(r)$ to first order on a fixed Gaussian model, so free covariates save at least $1/b$ rounds. A hybrid rule adds a label-history fallback for risk changes that leave the inputs unchanged. Synthetic experiments and two ACS tasks, with strengthened label-only baselines, show the predicted pattern.
